[QA COMPARE 01] Compare arteries and veins in terms of direction of blood flow and wall structure.
questions.answer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart and generally have thicker muscular walls; veins return blood and have thinner walls with valves.

questions.question: [QA COMPARE 02] Compare skeletal muscle and smooth muscle by control and appearance.
questions.answer: Skeletal muscle is voluntary and striated, while smooth muscle is involuntary and non-striated.

questions.question: [QA COMPARE 03] Compare DNA and RNA by sugar and usual cellular role.
[QA COMPARE 04] Compare competitive and noncompetitive enzyme inhibition.
questions.answer: Competitive inhibition affects the active site and can often be overcome by more substrate; noncompetitive inhibition binds elsewhere and reduces effective enzyme activity.

questions.question: [QA COMPARE 05] Compare Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial cell envelopes.
[QA ESSAY 01] Explain how the cardiac cycle produces forward blood flow.
questions.answer: Atrial and ventricular contractions occur in sequence, with valves opening and closing according to pressure differences.

questions.question: [QA ESSAY 02] Discuss the main functions of the liver in metabolism.
questions.answer: The liver processes nutrients, stores glycogen, synthesizes plasma proteins, produces bile, and detoxifies many compounds.

questions.question: [QA ESSAY 03] Describe the stages of wound healing.
[QA ESSAY 04] Explain why the alveolar surface is efficient for gas exchange.
questions.answer: It has a large surface area, a thin diffusion barrier, and close contact with pulmonary capillaries.

questions.question: [QA ESSAY 05] Describe how vaccination supports adaptive immunity.
[QA ANATOMY 01] Identify the boundaries and contents of the cubital fossa.
questions.answer: The cubital fossa is bounded by the brachioradialis and pronator teres with the elbow crease superiorly; it contains the biceps tendon, brachial artery, and median nerve in order from lateral to medial.

[QA MICROBIOLOGY 01] Explain two mechanisms by which bacteria may become resistant to antibiotics.
questions.answer: Mechanisms include drug-inactivating enzymes, altered targets, reduced permeability, and active efflux.
